To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the citizen journalists we interviewed in Turkey do not have any formal training or professional experience in journalism and they are not affiliated to any news organizations.
The majority of the Turkish citizen journalists are young, educated, and male.
the majority of the participants in our study are not satisfied with the current media landscape and are willing to participate in the production of news.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the new communication technologies have impacted the way journalism is practiced in Turkey, and the role of citizen journalists in the process
the following question: What role does citizen journalism play in Turkey’s media landscape?
the role that citizens can and do play in the news media, and the impact of their activities on the news media, as well as the impact of the news media on citizens’ activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
new media has the potential to change journalism and media work.
the impact of citizen journalism is still under debate.
the future of journalism is not yet determined and it is too early to predict what will happen in the near future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the citizen journalism is not a new form of journalism, it is a new way of doing the journalism.
citizen journalism is a form of participatory media that allows individuals to create and disseminate information to a broad audience through the internet and social networking platforms.
citizen journalism is an alternative to professional journalism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
citizen journalists are more likely to be active in the political process and to have more political efficacy, but they are also more likely to be exposed to political propaganda.
the media landscape is changing and that there is a need for a new media literacy that will help us navigate the new information environment.
the Turkish media landscape is suffocating and there is no room for independent journalism. However, there is hope for citizen journalism.
